steps.say: Every material has properties, such as hard, flexible, transparent or magnetic. We choose materials by their properties.
Most metals are shiny, strong and can be hammered into shape. They ring when you strike them.
Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity. That is why pans and wires are made of metal.
Wood, plastic, wool and air are thermal insulators. They slow down the flow of heat.
Only a few metals are magnetic, such as iron, nickel and steel. Copper, aluminium and gold are not.

figure.alt: A magnet with a steel paper clip and an iron nail, which are both magnetic.

steps.say: Graphite in pencils is a non-metal that conducts electricity. Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.

check.prompt: Why are electric wires made of copper?

options.why: Copper is not magnetic, and wires do not need to be.
Copper is opaque, like all metals.
Copper conducts heat well, so it is not an insulator.

hints: A wire must let electricity flow through it.
Materials that let electricity flow are called conductors.
Cross out the properties that have nothing to do with electricity.
check.explanation: Copper is an excellent conductor of electricity, and it can be pulled into thin wires. That makes it ideal for electric wires.

check.prompt: Which object would a magnet pick up?

options.why: Aluminium is a metal, but it is not magnetic.

hints: Only a few metals are magnetic.
Iron and steel are attracted to magnets.
Look for the object made of steel.
check.explanation: Steel is mostly iron, so a magnet attracts it. Aluminium, copper and plastic are not magnetic.
